paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so let me say it plain. At the time when kings march out to war, David sent out Joab and the army, but David remained in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1). From the roof he saw a woman, he sent messengers to get her, and soon a cover-up began (2 Samuel 11:2-6). One step led to another, and I think that's the warning, because that first look never showed where the road would end.

Watch what David does when the cover-up hits a wall. He gets Uriah drunk (2 Samuel 11:13), and when that doesn't work, he writes a letter that puts Uriah at the front of the fiercest battle (2 Samuel 11:15). Meanwhile Uriah won't go home while the ark and Israel are dwelling in tents (2 Samuel 11:11), so he is the one doing right in the middle of all this. And when David sends back, 'Do not let this matter upset you…' (2 Samuel 11:25), I think those calm words are the scary part, friend.

The passage ends with the line to carry out of here: 'But the thing that David had done was evil in the sight of the LORD.' (2 Samuel 11:27). David sent calm words to Joab, but the LORD's view is what the passage leaves us with. That's a hard word, and an honest one, because the LORD sees what we do for what it is. So take it seriously, friend, and stay close to the Word, because this story isn't over.
